evidence_note: Okoye & Mamven, Kidney360 3(9):1607-1610, 'Global Dialysis Perspective: Nigeria'. This 2021 total of centres (the paper cites its own ref 3) is much larger than the 80 units in the survey. "The number of centers increased from 27 in 2006 ... to 186 in 2021"

From an online survey of nephrology professionals in April-May 2022 (non-random, spread through a WhatsApp group; 103 responses, de-duplicated to 80 units). "The survey revealed a total hemodialysis population of 3050 spread across 80 actively functioning centers in Nigeria."

Table 1 ownership of the 80 surveyed units: 65% public, 24% private, 11% public-private (65% of 80 = 52, which matches the Nigeria Health Watch figure). Table 1 rows: "Public-owned units" 65; "Private-owned units" 24; "Public-private owned" 11

Federal government press release: an 11-hospital pilot of the dialysis subsidy. "Implementation of the pilot scheme is ongoing in the following eleven (11nos.) Federal Tertiary Health institutions"; "The price per dialysis session under the subsidy scheme, is now N12,000 as against the previous N50,000."

Nigeria Health Watch, citing the 'Global Dialysis Perspective: Nigeria' study (PMC9528372). "there are only 80 functioning haemodialysis centres across the country, of which 52 are public-owned centres"
Nigeria Health Watch repeats the total from the same study. "there are only 80 functioning haemodialysis centres across the country, of which 52 are public-owned centres"

UK Home Office CPIN (section 5.13.2), quoting the EUAA Medical COI report of April 2022, which says the centres have "varying levels of functionality". "There are dialysis centres – about 149 centres with 600 dialysis machines – across the 36 states in the country"

The Nephrology Association of Nigeria (NAN), via its president Prof. Awobusuyi, gives a lower bound of more than 200 functional dialysis units. "while Nigeria has over 200 functional dialysis units, only about 800 dialysis machines are operational nationwide"

World Kidney Day article giving the NAN figure for centres. It does not say whether all of them are functional. "Nigeria has over 200 dialysis centres and about 800 functional dialysis machines nationwide"

The Guardian says 10 subsidised centres at N12,000 per session. This conflicts with the 11 in the government release (see the separate rows). "the Federal Government last year subsidised the cost of dialysis at 10 centres nationwide" ... "bringing the cost down to N12,000 per session."
Gives machines per surveyed centre but no national total. Table 1: "Number of hemodialysis machines per center": "Mean" 4±1; "Range" 1–15
Equipment downtime is common because machines are old and poorly maintained. "Equipment downtime in many centers is a common challenge." ... "machines are old and often poorly maintained"

Same UK Home Office CPIN passage, quoting EUAA (April 2022); the functional status of the machines is unstated. "There are dialysis centres – about 149 centres with 600 dialysis machines – across the 36 states in the country"

Prof. Awobusuyi of the Nephrology Association of Nigeria gives the number of operational machines. "only about 800 dialysis machines are operational nationwide" The article says the total is "far short of the number needed to address the growing caseload."
World Kidney Day article giving the NAN figure for functional machines. "Nigeria has over 200 dialysis centres and about 800 functional dialysis machines nationwide"
An older count (2020), attributed by Nigeria Health Watch to the nephrologists' association. "Data from the association also reveals that only 160 nephrologists are practicing in Nigeria."
National workforce count; the paper also says brain drain threatens it. "there are only 240 nephrologists, 697 registered dialysis nurses (145 of these migrated to Western countries)"
Unreliable power supply affects dialysis units. "Other problems are frequent power interruptions, with poor and expensive backups."

Registered dialysis nurses. 145 of the 697 have migrated abroad, so the paper's figures imply about 552 remain (my subtraction). "697 registered dialysis nurses (145 of these migrated to Western countries)"
Dialysis technologists and technicians, national count. "120 dialysis technologists/technicians"

Haemodialysis patients per million people (Table 1, April 2022, N=3050). Caveat: 3050 divided by 200 million is about 15 per million, so the paper's own figures are inconsistent. Table 1: "17 per million people (N=3050)"
Share (%) of ESKD patients on haemodialysis (2018 data). "only 2% (3000) of Nigerian ESKD patients were receiving hemodialysis in 2018"

An estimate of the functional machines NEEDED, not machines that exist, given by Prof. Awobusuyi, immediate past NAN president. "Nigeria needs about 5000 functional dialysis machines to effectively cater for the growing number of patients"

Prof. Salako says the subsidy does not fully cover running costs. "other operational costs, such as electricity, water supply, and equipment maintenance" (the article reports these as not fully covered by the subsidy)
